key_insight: StateDRIFT tailors Hamiltonian-term sampling to the initial state and target observable, reducing estimator bias and variance while retaining qDRIFT’s guarantees through a provable truncation bound.
engineering_relevance: Problem-aware sampling can reduce the circuit depth and two-qubit gate count needed for accurate quantum-dynamics estimates.
method: Optimise the sampling distribution at each depth to target bias, variance, or both.
Use initial-state observables and commutators to guide sampling.
Estimate required quantities with classical surrogates such as tensor networks, or with classical shadows.
evidence_signal: Tests on short-time lattice and molecular dynamics up to 18 qubits included a BeH2 example reducing two-qubit gates from 11,201 to 983 at a given accuracy.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on the cost and accuracy of estimating the state-dependent quantities; evaluation here is limited to short-time dynamics.
paper_title: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
